title: Observability & Failure Modes in System Design

scenes.line1: How do you spot failures fast?
scenes.say: Ever wonder how big systems catch failures before users notice? Let's break down observability and failure modes.

scenes.label: Logging
scenes.sub: Logs, metrics, and tracing help you monitor system health and spot issues.
scenes.say: Observability means using logs, metrics, and traces to track how your system is doing. It's how you catch problems early.

rows.b: Serve partial features if dependencies fail

scenes.say: To handle failures, use timeouts to avoid stuck requests, circuit breakers to prevent overload, and graceful degradation to keep some features working even when parts break.

scenes.title: API fallback when DB fails
scenes.say: If your database goes down, your API can return cached data with a warning. After several failures, a circuit breaker stops more requests to let things recover.

scenes.question: What’s a common interview mistake here?
scenes.wrong: Just add logs and move on.
scenes.right: Logs alone aren’t enough. You need metrics, tracing, and failure handling patterns like circuit breakers and timeouts to build a reliable system.
scenes.say: A lot of candidates just mention logging. But interviewers want to hear about metrics, tracing, and patterns like circuit breakers and timeouts.
